title: General Services Administration: Volt Information Sciences, Inc. - 2013 Suspension & Debarment Division Deliberations

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: General Services Administration: Volt Information Sciences, Inc. - 2013 Suspension & Debarment Division Deliberations
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request all correspondence, integrity reviews, contractor responsibility assessments, or FAPIIS/SAM.gov exclusion-check documentation referencing Volt Information Sciences, Inc. or its subsidiaries and affiliates — including Volt Telecommunications Group, Inc. and Volt Management Corp. — created between January 20, 2009, and January 1, 2015, in connection with:

1. GSA Federal Supply Schedule Contract No. GS35F0552L (IT Schedule 70), held by Volt Telecommunications Group, Inc., including any Contractor Assessment, eligibility review, or administrative correspondence referencing SEC Litigation Release No. 22589, the SEC's January 2013 accounting-fraud charges against Volt Information Sciences, Inc., or the company's related 2011 delisting from the New York Stock Exchange; and

2. Public Buildings Service Contract No. GSP0412EW0085 (security system repair, DHS/ICE Office of Principal Legal Advisor, Hollister Building, Orlando, FL), including the contracting officer's responsibility determination and any related correspondence.

For context, the SEC released Litigation Release No. 22589 in 2013: https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/litigation-releases/lr-22589 The public findings by the SEC would have undoubtedly created debate within the GSA as to the federal government's relationship with Volt Information Sciences, Inc. and its subsidiaries and affiliates. These files are likely held by the Suspension & Debarment Division within GSA. 

Search terms: "Volt Information Sciences" OR "Volt Telecommunications Group" OR "Volt Management Corp" OR "Volt Delta Resources" combined with "Litigation Release No. 22589" OR "accounting restatement" OR "revenue
recognition" OR "debarment" OR "suspension" OR "responsibility determination"

Please include a search of the subject line, body, or attachments of any emails sent to the uspension-and-debarment@gsa.gov email address between January 20th 2009 and January 1st 2015 for the above search terms. 

I request classification as a representative of the news media the purpose of this request is to preserve documentation related to Volt and Litigation Release No. 22589 in order to inform the public. 

Thank you to the General Services Administration and I look forward to working together on this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: SEC: Litigation Release No. 22589 / January 11, 2013 - Investigation of Volt Information Sciences, Inc.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: SEC: Litigation Release No. 22589 / January 11, 2013 - Investigation of Volt Information Sciences, Inc.
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request copies of the investigative file compiled by the Division of Enforcement in connection with:

● The Matter Under Inquiry / investigation of Volt Information Sciences, Inc. disclosed as opened on or about November 8, 2010, and

● Securities and Exchange Commission v. Volt Information Sciences, Inc. and Debra L. Hobbs, No. 13-CV-237 (S.D.N.Y.), and Securities and Exchange Commission v. Jack J. Egan, Jr., No. 13-CV-236 (S.D.N.Y.) (Litigation Release No.  22589 / January 11, 2013; AAER No. 3439)

The litigation release is online, here: https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/litigation-releases/lr-22589

This request includes, but is not limited to: the Formal Order of Investigation and any amendments; Wells notices and Wells submissions; staff action memoranda recommending charges or settlement; internal correspondence regarding the scope or theory of the case; and any referral to or from other federal agencies (including any criminal referral to the Department of Justice).

I request classification as a representative of the news media, as I am this request is made for the purpose of public dissemination of the resulting records. Accordingly, I request a waiver of search fees and the first 100 pages of duplication fees. If fees beyond that are anticipated to exceed $50.00, please provide an itemized estimate before proceeding.

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(b), please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt material, and for any withholding, identify the specific FOIA exemption invoked for each redacted or withheld record.

Thank you for the work that the Securities and Exchange Commission does each day, and thank for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: Colonial Auto Body Shop Inc., 5 Rawson Rd — Spray Booth, Flammable Liquid and Spill Records

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Colonial Auto Body Shop Inc., 5 Rawson Rd — Spray Booth, Flammable Liquid and Spill Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:


Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I am requesting the following records from the Hanover Fire Department concerning Colonial Auto Body Shop Inc., located at 5 Rawson Rd, Hanover, MA 02339:

1.	Spray booth permits and associated permit files.
2.	Flammable liquid permits and associated permit files.
3.	Tier II Emergency and Hazardous Chemical Inventory reports and related filings.
4.	Fire Department incident reports and spill reports for the property.

Please search using both the facility name and address, including responsive historical records maintained under former business or operator names at this address.


I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. 

Electronic copies provided through this MuckRock request or a secure download link are preferred. Where available, please provide searchable PDFs or other accessible electronic formats.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Vlad Gaylun
